findings.title: Passkey check is inverted: it now needs a user, so first login never gets conditional passkeys.
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns true only when `user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn data when no user was selected (`context.getUser() == null`). Both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) now call this helper, so a normal first login with no user identified never calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. The login page loses the conditional passkey UI and the `webauth` form, and it also loses them after a failed password attempt. The tests in this PR expect that form on the first login page (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest lines 196 and 238). The `user != null` term also shows passkeys on re-authentication to users who have no passkey credential. Fix: enable passkeys when no user is selected, or when the selected user has a passwordless credential, e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()))`.

held.title: Call to a no-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that the shown code does not define.
held.body: This change adds only `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` to `UsernamePasswordForm`. `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. If no no-argument overload exists somewhere I cannot see, this does not compile. If one does exist, it ignores the current user: whenever passkeys are on for the realm, every re-authenticating user gets the username form, including users with no passkey. Pass `context.getUser()` so this matches the sibling class.
